We need to produce final answer. Provide list of precursors. Ensure correct SMILES. Let's double-check the target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Break at C(=O)N bond. The carbonyl carbon is attached to the alkene chain and to the N which is attached to phenyl with NH2. So acid fragment: the part containing carbonyl carbon, alkene, aromatic sulfonyl phenyl, and methyl phenyl. Replace N with OH to make carboxylic acid. So acid SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1

Check: original had .../C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . So after replacement, .../C=C/C(=O)O . Yes.

Amine fragment: Nc3ccccc3 . That's an aniline with NH attached to phenyl. SMILES: Nc1ccccc1 . The original had N attached to phenyl and also has an extra N? Actually the fragment is Nc3ccccc3N meaning the phenyl has an NH2? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" means N attached to phenyl, and phenyl has an N substituent? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is ambiguous: It is N attached to aromatic carbon (position 1) and the aromatic ring also has an N substituent at another position? The SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline with an extra N at the end? Let's parse: "c3ccccc3" is phenyl. Preceded by N: "N c3ccccc3 N". That means an aniline where the phenyl has an N attached at both ends? Actually SMILES: "Nc3ccccc3N" means N attached to aromatic carbon (position 1) and also the aromatic carbon at position 6 attached to N (since after the ring closure, there is N). So it's a phenyl diamine (p-phenylenediamine) but with N attached at both ends? The ring has two substituents: one N (the amide N) attached to carbonyl, and another N (primary amine) attached to the ring. So the amine fragment after cleavage would be the aniline with an extra NH2? The fragment is "Nc3ccccc3N" which is p-phenylenediamine? Actually the SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" corresponds to aniline with an extra N at the other end (para). So the fragment is a diamine: 1,4-diaminobenzene (p-phenylenediamine). SMILES for p-phenylenediamine: N c1ccc(cc1) N . That's "Nc1ccc(cc1)N". So we should use that.

Thus amine precursor SMILES: Nc1ccc(cc1)N

Check: The original N attached to carbonyl is the same as one of the N's on the phenyl. So after cleavage, we have the phenyl with two amine groups: one is the amide N now free (primary amine) and the other is the existing NH2. So the amine fragment is p-phenylenediamine.

Thus final precursors: acid fragment and p-phenylenediamine.

Acid SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1

Amine SMILES: Nc1ccc(cc1)N

Return list of list: [["Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1", "Nc1ccc(cc1)N"]]
